title: Version 3 gives one recovery schema, not the target schema of each table
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Approach v3.docx
description: Version 3 names one recovery schema as the landing place of every migrated table and never names the target service or schema of a single table. Arch v5 gives one schema per service, so the document cannot say which of the 19 schemas receives recovery_case, treatment, document, decision_log_entry, partner or the reference tables.
evidence: v3 section 2 line 32 (nothing of them moves into the recovery schema); v3 section 5 line 74 (six of the fourteen stories change, the other eight keep their scope); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 4 (every service has schema rwb_<name> plus DB login) and slide 8 line 635 (19 rwb_* schemas, one login each); ADR-014; DP-01.
proposed: Each migrated table lands in the schema of its owner in Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables; section 9.2 lists the tables and the schema of each.

title: The owner-side migration step has no story ID
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Approach v3.docx
description: The 14 migration stories are P1 rwb-source-data work (plus the ITG and P8 copies in the plan) and describe the extract, the key mapping and the reconciliation. No story carries the load of a table into the schema of its owner, and version 3 cannot name one because it has no per-schema step.
evidence: v3 section 5 line 74 and the six rows below it; plan/split_plan.json legacy entries RWB-DM-003 to RWB-DM-014 (primary P1, one P8 copy on DM-013); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 (one contract per service) and slide 20; DP-15 per-service Flyway; ADR-021.
proposed: The owner-side load is the service's own Flyway step under RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, run in the same cutover step as the P1 extract story; no story ID is invented and the delta is recorded against the owning service's story set.

title: Version 3 has the Workbench run the load; the target makes the schema owner run it
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Approach v3.docx
description: Version 3 describes each migration as a Workbench extract and load into its own schema, run by the recovery service identity. Arch v5 gives each service its own schema, login and Flyway sequence, and DP-01 forbids one service writing another service's tables, so the loading identity and the place of the extract change for all 14 stories.
evidence: v3 section 1 How column lines 21 to 27 (spreadsheet extract, file extract, bulk intake through OCR, partner master load); v3 section 3 line 53 (every migrated record carries its source and migration date); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 8 line 635 and slide 20 (outbox and relay per service); ADR-021; DP-01; DP-15.
proposed: Extract, key mapping and reconciliation stay with rwb-source-data (P1); the load is the owner's Flyway step in the owner's schema, run by the owner's migrator login created by RWB-PLT-N011-DB; P1 never writes another schema.

title: Reference data is one load in version 3 and six schemas in the Ownership Map
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Approach v3.docx
section: 1. What moves (Reference data row); 5. Migration stories
description: Version 3 treats reference data (DP14) as one validated load with one landing place, and the R-PREC default ruling gives parameters and reference data to P3. The Ownership Map splits DP14 across five services: parameters and lists of values to P3, rule packages to P7, roles and DoA limits to P4, templates to P6, document types and retention to P5, and the EFS action codes to P1. One story (RWB-DM-014) cannot load six schemas by itself.
evidence: v3 section 1 line 27 (Reference data, DP14, validated load, versioned); Template and Rules R3 default ruling (parameters and reference data to P3 rwb-case; rule package registry to P7 rwb-decision); Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables rows lov_value, rule_package, delegation_limit, role, template, document_type, retention_rule, efs_ledger_outcome; Ownership Map v1 sheet Parameters.
proposed: RWB-P1-DM014-APP extracts and validates; each owner schema loads and versions its own reference tables as listed in section 9.4.

title: The expected-return and sale-estimate records have no table and no schema
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Approach v3.docx
description: Version 3 says that only the expected-return and sale-estimate records the Workbench calculates move for RWB-DM-011, but names no table for them. The story data table names case_list_row and measure_snapshot only, so neither the table nor the schema of these records is specified.
evidence: v3 section 5 line 82 (only the expected-return and sale-estimate records the Workbench calculates move); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Stories v3.md RWB-DM-011 Data table (case_list_row, measure_snapshot); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 18 (rwb_valuation writes valuations, the D6 route decision and the route agent output); Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables (no table for expected return or sale estimate).
proposed: The records are held in the rwb_valuation route-decision output (S1); the case_list_row and measure_snapshot parts stay with P1 and P9.

title: All 14 migration stories are wave 4 while nine services are wave 1
section: 6. Parallel run; 7. Reconciliation and the cut-over check
description: Every migration story is in wave 4 with a release of 30 November 2026 or 31 December 2026, while P1, P3, P4, P5, P6, P7, P9 and P10 and the rest of wave 1 go live in wave 1. Version 3 ties the parallel run to each team's first release, which cannot hold if the schema of a wave 1 service is only loaded in wave 4.
evidence: plan/split_plan.json slices RWB-P1-DM003-APP to RWB-P1-DM014-APP and RWB-ITG-DM003-ITG to RWB-ITG-DM013-ITG (wave 4, releases 30 November 2026 and 31 December 2026); Ownership Map v1 sheet Services (waves 1 to 4); Template and Rules R5.6 W-MAP and R5.7 Day-1 rules.
proposed: Each schema cuts over in the wave of its owning service, using the order in section 9.5; the migration story releases stay as they are and are read as the latest date, not the earliest.

title: No retention period and no owner for the legacy Workbench tables after cutover
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Approach v3.docx
section: 6. Parallel run; 7. Reconciliation and the cut-over check
description: Version 3 says the spreadsheet retires when the business lead signs ten clean days and, in the story set, that the legacy tables stay read-only for their retention period. It states no retention period, no retention class and no owner for the legacy Workbench tables once a schema has cut over.
evidence: v3 section 6 line 88 (the spreadsheet retires when the business lead signs ten clean days); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Stories v3.md RWB-DM-003 AC3 (the legacy tables stay read-only for their retention period); Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables row retention_rule (P5); DP-01.
proposed: Legacy tables stay read-only in place for the retention class of their content under the P5 retention_rule; the data steward signs each schema's cutover before the archive date is set.

title: The custody of migrated document originals is not assigned
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Approach v3.docx
description: Version 3 says documents for open cases are taken in by bulk intake through OCR with originals tracked, but not where the originals are held after the migration, which service owns the custody rows, or what happens to files already in the shared drives and the mailroom.
evidence: v3 section 1 line 24 (Documents, DP10, bulk intake through OCR, originals tracked); v3 section 3 line 57 (spreadsheets are retired with a read-only archive); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (rwb-document writes metadata, custody, OCR text and fields; FILE Azure Blob WORM) and slide 8 (Blob WORM); Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables rows document, document_custody (P5).
proposed: Originals go to Blob WORM through rwb-document only; metadata and every custody movement are rows in rwb_document.document and document_custody.

title: The target table of the open promises and contact notes is not named
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Approach v3.docx
description: Version 3 reduces RWB-DM-005 to the open promises and contact notes held outside EFS, but names no table and no schema for them. The story data table names interaction and contact_point_ext, which the approach document never mentions.
evidence: v3 section 5 line 80 (only the open promises and contact notes held outside EFS move); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Stories v3.md RWB-DM-005 Data table (interaction, contact_point_ext); Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables rows interaction and contact_point_ext (P1); DP-18 interaction ledger default ruling.
proposed: Open promises and contact notes land in rwb_source_data.interaction, with the consent flags in contact_point_ext; EFS history stays a read through v_ace_efs_action.
